t.1.19.1: Then, when the night had given way to dawn and the sun had risen in the morning, O ascetic rich in austerities, those two sisters, Kadrū and Vinatā,
t.1.19.3: Then the two of them beheld there the ocean, the treasury of waters, teeming with timiṅgilas and fish and likewise thronged with makaras.
t.1.19.2: Then the two, indignant and greatly enraged, having made a wager with slavery as the stake, went to see the horse Uccaiḥśravas up close.
t.1.19.4: It was surrounded by many thousands of creatures of various forms, fierce ones, so that it was ever unassailable, and it teemed with tortoises and crocodiles.
t.1.19.5: They beheld the ocean, the mine of all jewels and the abode of Varuṇa, the delightful dwelling of the Nāgas, the supreme lord of rivers.
t.1.19.6: They beheld the ocean, the abode of the fire of Pātāla and the prison of the Asuras, terrifying to living creatures, the great treasury of the waters.
t.1.19.7: They beheld it auspicious and divine, the supreme mine of the nectar of the immortals, immeasurable and inconceivable, wondrous, with waters most holy.
t.1.19.9: They saw the ocean, tossing with winds that swung its shores like a swing, risen up in agitation and turmoil, as if dancing on every side with its waves for hands, moving restlessly.
t.1.19.8: Dreadful, fierce with the cries of its water-dwelling creatures, with a terrifying roar, teeming with deep whirlpools, frightening to all beings.
t.1.19.10: the ocean, hard to approach with its waves surging up under the sway of the moon's waxing and waning, the birthplace of Pāñcajanya, the unsurpassed mine of jewels.
t.1.19.11: It was turbid with waters stirred up within it by the blessed Govinda of boundless might, who, in the form of a boar, was finding the earth.
t.1.19.12: Its bottom was never reached even by the brahmarṣi Atri, though he practiced austerities for a hundred years; imperishable, it extends down to the very floor of Pātāla.
t.1.19.14: The auspicious lord of rivers, which offers its waters as oblation to the blazing fire of Vaḍavāmukha, fathomless, its farther shore beyond reach, vast and immeasurable.
t.1.19.13: It was the couch, at the dawn of the yugas, of Padmanābha, Viṣṇu of boundless splendor, as he gives himself over to the yogic sleep of the supreme self.
t.1.19.15: The two of them beheld the great ocean, ceaselessly sought out by many great rivers in their thousands, as if in rivalry with one another.
t.1.19.17: Thus beholding that ocean, crowded with fish, makara monsters and waves, deep, wide-spread, shining like the sky, and lit up by the flames of the fire of Pātāla, the two then swiftly flew onward.
t.1.19.16: The two women beheld that ocean, deep and teeming with fierce timis and makaras, roaring with the dreadful cries of its water-dwelling creatures, wide-spread and shining like the sky, the fathomless, vast and endless treasury of the waters.
